2012.note: District 30's general-election result is missing from the state's file (a special primary for the seat was held the same day); the seat stayed Republican, so the Senate stood at 38 R, 18 D.

2020.note: District 39 is missing: its Democratic nominee was chosen in a special primary after the original nominee withdrew; the seat stayed Democratic, so the Senate stood at 34 R, 22 D.

2018.note: Districts 14 and 28 are missing from the state's file (both Republican; the District 28 result was voided and rerun in 2019), so the House stood at 105 R, 75 D.

notes.source: 2000-2010: OpenElections Georgia files, transcribed from the Secretary of State's certified results. 2012-2025: the Secretary of State's official results system (results.sos.ga.gov), summed from its county results. 2026: the live state feed on this page.
caveats: District lines changed several times (after the 2000, 2010 and 2020 censuses, by court order in 2004, mid-decade for Congress in 2005, and again in late 2023 for 2024), so a district number does not always cover the same area from one election to the next.
Runoffs are listed separately from the general election that preceded them.
2020 presidential figures are the state's first certification; the recount certification on Dec. 7, 2020 changed the statewide totals by under 0.02 percentage points.
Georgia's city elections are nonpartisan, so party comparisons are only possible for partisan county offices and for state and federal races.
